title: Amazon Shopping on Fire TV
jpTitle: Fire TV 向け Amazon ショッピング
summary: A self-built proof of concept reimagining Amazon shopping for a 10-foot TV interface: D-pad browsing, Alexa-style voice shopping, and a paired phone that becomes remote, keyboard and mic via a QR-code pairing layer. Built solo with vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, Firebase and the Web Speech API. Not affiliated with Amazon; product data and voice replies are simulated.

angles.creative-tech: A pairing protocol — QR or 6-character code, presence heartbeat, room cleanup — built once for this TV prototype and then extracted into a separate open-source library used elsewhere.
angles.product: Three long-standing 10-foot-UI problems — slow remote text entry, voice with no visual context, and browsing fatigue — resolved by giving the phone the keyboard, pointer and mic job and leaving the TV as the display.

mine: Designed a 10-foot commerce interface where the TV is the stage and the phone is the input device
Built D-pad navigation for discovery and Alexa-style voice for intent
Built a phone-as-remote web app (keyboard, precise pointer, private mic) with instant QR pairing, no download or login
Built on own open-source 'snap-pair' pairing pattern — QR/6-character code, presence heartbeat, room membership, cleanup
Mirrored cart, screen and search state to the phone in real time
Built the entire prototype solo — vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, Firebase and the Web Speech API

metrics.label: input modes unified: D-pad, voice, phone remote
scan to pair — no app install required

narrative.problem: Shopping on a TV should feel effortless from the couch, but text entry is painful, browsing with a tiny remote is slow, and voice alone can't always show enough context — the experience gets stuck between 'lean-back' convenience and 'lean-in' detail.
built: Phone-as-remote web app (D-pad / trackpad / joystick / mic)
